title: Lower limb midterm · 24 January 2023
note: TUMS cover says Midterm Exam, Dr Pasbakhsh, 24 January 2023 (despite a February-semester label). Optional supplement, not mislabeled as a final. Annotated copies share this record. Original Q31 has an incomplete stem and is preserved ungraded.

questions.prompt: All of the following muscles attach to femur EXCEPT:
questions.note: Sartorius runs from ASIS to medial proximal tibia, not femur.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All of the following muscles attach to fibula EXCEPT:
questions.note: Tibialis anterior arises on tibia/interosseous membrane. The other muscles have fibular origins.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All of the following muscles attach to hip bone EXCEPT:
questions.note: Popliteus connects distal femur/lateral meniscal relations to posterior tibia.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All of the following are found on femur EXCEPT:
questions.note: Soleal line is on posterior tibia.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All of the following muscles are femoral-supplied EXCEPT:
questions.note: Gracilis is supplied by obturator nerve.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which muscle attaches to the inferomedial surface of the superior half of the ischial tuberosity?
questions.note: Semitendinosus/long-head biceps share the inferomedial part of the upper area; semimembranosus is superolateral.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All of these spinal nerves participate in the lumbar plexus EXCEPT:
questions.note: The standard lumbar plexus is L1–4 with possible T12 contribution; L5 enters the sacral plexus via lumbosacral trunk.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All of these nerves belong to the sacral plexus EXCEPT:
questions.note: Obturator derives from L2–4 lumbar plexus.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All of these muscles are tibial-supplied EXCEPT:
questions.note: Fibularis longus is superficial fibular-supplied.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All of these muscles are deep-peroneal-supplied EXCEPT:
questions.note: Both A (tibial nerve) and D (lateral plantar nerve) are exceptions. This source has two correct answers; both are accepted.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which nerve supplies medial cutaneous surface of the leg?
questions.note: Saphenous is the femoral sensory continuation to medial leg.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All these muscles attach to calcaneus EXCEPT:
questions.note: FHL originates on fibula and inserts on distal hallux; its tendon passes near calcaneus without a bony attachment.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which artery supplies the dorsomedial margin of the second toe?
options: Second dorsal metatarsal branch of arcuate
questions.note: First dorsal metatarsal supplies adjacent sides of hallux and second toe dorsally.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct?
options: Saphenous opening is in fascia lata
Great saphenous drains to popliteal vein
Medial meniscus attaches to fibular collateral ligament
questions.note: Saphenous opening is in fascia lata. Great saphenous drains to femoral; dorsal interossei number four.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: What is the function of gluteus maximus?
questions.note: Hip extension is its principal tested action; lower fibers may also adduct, so this is a main-action interpretation.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All are lateral rotators of thigh at hip EXCEPT:
questions.note: Semimembranosus extends hip and medially rotates the flexed leg.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All participate in cruciate anastomosis EXCEPT:
questions.note: The standard network also includes medial circumflex femoral; popliteal is not a component.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which lies immediately medial to tibialis posterior tendon in the tarsal tunnel?
questions.note: The intended adjacent structure is FDL. The source directional term is imprecise: the standard anterior-to-posterior order begins tibialis posterior, FDL, vessels, nerve, FHL.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which muscle attaches to cuboid?
questions.note: FHB has a plantar cuboid/lateral cuneiform origin.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All are medial-plantar-supplied EXCEPT:
questions.note: Adductor hallucis is deep lateral plantar-supplied.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Coxa valga describes a femoral neck-shaft angle that is:
questions.note: Coxa valga is an increased inclination angle; normal reference varies with age.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All these ligaments attach to tibia EXCEPT:
questions.note: Fibular collateral connects femur to fibular head.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct?
options: Tibia has three borders and four surfaces
questions.note: Tibial nutrient supply typically comes from posterior tibial artery; shaft has three surfaces and lateral malleolus is fibular.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which nerve supplies the mediodorsal border of the fourth toe?
questions.note: Superficial fibular generally supplies this proximal dorsal region; distal nail-bed territories can have plantar supply.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Arcuate line is seen on which bone?
questions.note: Arcuate line is on the internal ilium.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which joint is a hinge joint?
questions.note: The knee is a modified hinge/bicondylar synovial joint.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which muscle attaches to base of fifth metatarsal?
questions.note: Fibularis tertius inserts on its dorsal base; fibularis brevis is another attachment but is not listed.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: A positive Trendelenburg sign indicates weakness of which muscles?
questions.note: Medius and minimus stabilize the contralateral pelvis in single-leg stance.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which muscle inverts the foot?
questions.note: Tibialis anterior is a dorsiflexor and invertor.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Sustentaculum tali is on which bone?
questions.note: The medial calcaneal shelf supports the talus.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All the following matches are correct except:
questions.note: No paired matches or other predicate are printed. There is no defensible answer without inventing the missing comparison. Original item retained, not graded.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Cuboid articulates with which metatarsals?
questions.note: Cuboid has anterior facets for fourth and fifth metatarsal bases.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Hallucal sesamoid bones lie in the tendon of:
questions.note: The two principal hallucal sesamoids lie in the two FHB tendons; FHL passes between them.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Adductor hiatus is formed in which muscle?
questions.note: The hiatus is an opening in distal adductor magnus for femoral vessels.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All these muscles attach to medial tibia EXCEPT:
questions.note: Biceps inserts mainly on fibular head; the first three form pes anserinus.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which two muscles share a nerve source?
questions.note: Superior gemellus is supplied by nerve to obturator internus; inferior gemellus by nerve to quadratus femoris.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Femoral triangle floor includes all EXCEPT:
questions.note: Sartorius is the lateral boundary and overlies the canal, not the triangle floor.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: The roof of the sulcus tali region is formed by:
questions.note: The intended sinus-tarsi roof is talar; sulcus tali itself is the groove on inferior talus.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which forms the posterior margin of the greater sciatic foramen?
questions.note: Sacrotuberous is posterior; sacrospinous defines the lower boundary.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: The female subpubic angle is approximately:
questions.note: A is the widest and intended listed answer. Female pubic arches are generally wider than male, commonly described around or above 80–90 degrees; this is not a universal exact interval.
questions.subject: anatomy
